title: Client-signature microbench for KV quant calibration and runtime profile routing
creator: Maya Patel
description: Run targeted KV cache quantization experiments that map lightweight client prompt signatures to per-client quant profiles. Build a microbench harness that replays realistic client distributions (long-tail prompts, code vs. dialog, varied sequence lengths) to validate INT8 and FP8 calibration workflows and measure latency/quality trade-offs. The goal is to decide a safe hybrid routing policy: aggressive low-precision for well-calibrated signatures, conservative FP16 fallback for uncalibrated or high-risk signatures.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Microbench can ingest a 1M-request sample and produce per-signature calibration suggestions. 2) We have measured median and 99.9th tail latency for FP8/INT8 vs FP16 for at least 5 client signature buckets. 3) Accuracy validation (semantic-similarity + task-specific metrics) completed for top-10 signatures and documented. 4) A rollout plan with automatic rollback thresholds and sampling rules is created.
experiment_plan: 1) Instrument dataset extraction to compute prompt fingerprints (first-50-token hash, task tag heuristics). 2) Select 20 high-volume signatures + 10 random low-volume signatures. 3) For each signature: run calibration sweep (per-token percentile clipping, outlier head handling) to produce INT8 and FP8 KV profiles. 4) Use microbench to replay requests to a shadow runtime with profile-selector routing. 5) Collect latency percentiles (p50, p95, p99, p999), token throughput (tokens/s), and quality metrics (semantic-similarity, ROUGE-L for summarization, pass@1 for code). 6) Run A/B and canary plan: shadow compare, 1% live test with traffic steering, rollback on quality regression >1.5% or p999 increase >40%.
metrics: latency_ms_p50, latency_ms_p95, latency_ms_p99, latency_ms_p999, tokens_per_second, semantic_similar_pct, rouge_l, pass_at_1, model_confidence_delta
results_summary: Preliminary microbench (shadow only) for 10k replayed requests per signature: FP8 profiles increased throughput by 1.9–2.3x and reduced median latency 12–18% compared to FP16. INT8 aggressive profiles reduced token compute by ~2.5x but caused 99.9th tail latency to spike for long sequences (>1024) unless KV fallback gating used. Accuracy: average semantic-similarity drop of 0.9% for conversational signatures, but code-completion signatures showed a larger degradation (~4.6% drop in pass@1) under INT8 aggressive profiles. Observed outlier heads on 3/20 signatures that required per-head clamp during calibration.
decisions: 1) Implement hybrid runtime routing: per-signature profile map with 'aggressive' (INT8 fastpath), 'conservative' (FP8), and 'safe' (FP16) buckets. 2) Default unknown signatures to 'conservative' and sample 0.5% into 'aggressive' for continued monitoring. 3) Add a p999 latency safety gate: if profile increases client p999 beyond 30% relative to baseline, auto-roll to 'safe' for that signature and create an alert.
next_steps: 1) Finalize calibration harness and add per-head clamp knobs. 2) Expand microbench to 1M requests overnight and collect full metrics. 3) Build automated profile exporter to runtime config store and a tooling page in Console for profile visibility. 4) Schedule 1% live canary for 7 days after QA signoff.
